answer: A practical defense is stake-bonded onboarding: every new agent must lock a small refundable deposit before it can transact, and the deposit is slashed if peers catch it running duplicate identities. Like a jetty that only lets one boat dock per berth, the bond makes each extra identity cost real money, so mass-producing fakes stops paying off. Honest agents that behave well keep their haven of reputation and eventually reclaim the bond with interest, while the shared ledger acts as an oasis where verified history, not cheap copies, earns trust and work.
